In the NVX-204 trial testing peloxatril against placebo (E1), 240 participants were enrolled in each arm (E2). 

In the peloxatril arm, 96 of 240 participants achieved at least a 50% reduction in monthly migraine days (E2, E3), which gives a responder rate of 40% (96 ÷ 240 = 0.40). 

In the placebo arm, 60 of 240 participants met the same 50% reduction threshold (E2, E4). Dividing 60 by 240 equals 0.25 (or 1/4), resulting in a responder rate of 25% (not 18%, which is an arithmetic error in some other responses). 

Subtracting the placebo rate from the peloxatril rate (40% − 25%) yields an absolute difference of 15 percentage points.

Answer: Peloxatril responder rate was 40%, placebo responder rate was 25%, and the absolute difference is 15 percentage points.
